what: Incorporating the BDC Public Data API
title: Process FCC data
text: FCC’s National Broadband Map exposes public REST API (documented https://us-fcc.app.box.com/v/bdc-public-data-api-swagger) offers structured alternative bulk download workflow currently implemented data-raw/. Three endpoints directly relevant ingestion pipeline. GET /api/public/map/listAsOfDates returns every available release date availability challenge data types. programmatic replacement get_nbm_release(), currently scrapes separate filing endpoint. GET /api/public/map/downloads/listAvailabilityData/{as_of_date} returns full manifest given release — including stable numeric file_id, file_name, record_count, state_fips, provider_id, category metadata every downloadable file. replaces get_nbm_available() , crucially, provides information currently reconstructed hand inconsistent FCC filename patterns (100-line normalization block data-raw/nbm_raw.R repairs December20ec_, June20un_, abbreviated date codes like D22/J23). GET /api/public/map/downloads/downloadFile/availability/{file_id}/1 downloads file stable numeric ID rather constructed URL. Combined manifest’s as_of_date field, release date embedded DuckDB strptime(split_part(filename, '_', 7), '%B%Y') expression simply passed directly, eliminating filename-based date parsing. manifest’s record_count field also enables meaningful post-download validation current file-presence check: row counts loaded DuckDB can compared API’s declared counts committing partition. manifest date-scoped, comparing already-ingested parquet partitions makes incremental ingestion (downloading new releases) straightforward implement. API endpoints require username hash_value request header. token generated via NBM web interface https://broadbandmap.fcc.gov/login Manage API Access, recommended approach storing R keyring. fcc_provider table (currently fetched hardcoded Box URL data-raw/fcc_provider.R) exposed BDC API remain unchanged.

what: Background: SSL error with dot-named S3 buckets
title: Process FCC data
text: late 2025, duckdb R package began producing SSL certificate errors reading parquet files S3 buckets whose names contain dots (e.g., cori.data.bds). root cause hostname mismatch: AWS’s virtual-hosted URL style turns cori.data.bds subdomain cori.data.bds.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com, many labels AWS’s wildcard TLS certificate (*.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com covers one subdomain level). error surfaced : fix one DuckDB setting switches URL construction virtual-hosted style path style, routing requests https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/... instead: Although cori.data.fcc (dots bucket name) directly affected SSL error, setting applied across functions package consistency rest coriverse.
code: SSL peer certificate or SSH remote key was not OK error for HTTP GET to 'https://cori.data.bds.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/...' DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET s3_url_style = 'path';")

previous_headings: DuckDB httpfs Configuration — Changelog and Notes
what: Background: HTTP timeout failures in DuckDB 1.4.4+
title: Process FCC data
text: applying SSL fix, new class errors appeared test suite functions query S3 directly via DuckDB’s httpfs extension (primarily get_frn_nbm_bl, scans state-level parquet partitions find rows matching given FRN): http_timeout setting defaults 30 seconds applies per HTTP request, per query. Reading single large state parquet file S3 requires multiple HTTP range requests (footer metadata, individual row groups), DuckDB 1.4.4 behaviour built-httplib HTTP client changed ways increased per-request latency — particularly documented duckdb/duckdb-java#548 (https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-java/issues/548). Additionally, httpfs_connection_caching defaults false, meaning every range request opens fresh TCP + TLS connection s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com rather reusing already-negotiated session.
code: IO Error: Timeout was reached error for HTTP GET to 'https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/cori.data.fcc/nbm_block-J24/state_abbr=AR/data_0.parquet'

previous_headings: DuckDB httpfs Configuration — Changelog and Notes
what: Changes applied to all httpfs connections in this package
title: Process FCC data
text: Three settings now explicitly configured every DuckDB connection uses httpfs extension: httpfs_client_implementation = 'curl' switches DuckDB built-httplib implementation libcurl, different case reliable code path S3 range requests. system curl binary already used successfully elsewhere package (download_file) underlying library known work network environment. http_timeout = 120 gives individual HTTP range request 120 seconds timing , 30-second default. backstop genuinely slow responses rather fix . httpfs_connection_caching = true enables connection pooling, sequential range requests S3 host reuse already-established TLS session. Without , 100+ HTTP range requests across full state partition scan incurs full TCP handshake TLS negotiation, adding hundreds milliseconds overhead per request.
code: DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET httpfs_client_implementation = 'curl';") DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET http_timeout = 120;") DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET httpfs_connection_caching = true;")

what: Why queries are still slower than they were in mid-2025
title: Process FCC data
text: Even settings applied, S3 queries via httpfs noticeably slower roughly six months prior. several likely contributing factors. DuckDB’s httpfs extension updated repeatedly across v1.4 v1.5 release series (bumped v1.5.2 v1.5.3 release notes), default HTTP client implementation changed ways affect connection setup range request behaviour. BDC data releases grown — D25 parquet files larger J24 files FCC adds reported locations cycle — directly increases amount data DuckDB must read per state partition. Finally, get_frn_nbm_bl performs full scan across 57 state territory partitions (s3://cori.data.fcc/nbm_block-{release}/*/*.parquet) FRN map partition key, every new row data added partition adds incremental cost every call. local-cache pattern used get_nbm_bl get_nbm_county (syncing relevant state via aws s3 sync querying disk) avoids problem entirely recommended approach repeated latency-sensitive queries.
